title: The Raynor Stack
subtitle: How abundant intelligence might become humane, continuous and inhabitable
author: Raynor Eissens
central_question: How can we live with increasingly abundant intelligence without surrendering human time and attention?
thesis: The layers are cumulative: each layer changes how the earlier layers are experienced, and failures at an earlier layer propagate upward.

definitions.Time: The finite continuity in which a life, project or institution can develop.
definitions.Attention: The limited capacity to notice, choose and care within available time.
definitions.AI: Machine intelligence used to carry context, compare possibilities and perform work; evaluated partly by the attention it returns.
definitions.Warmth: Room for care, judgment, play and presence made possible when technology supports rather than exhausts.
definitions.Ambience: Support distributed through surroundings instead of confined to one explicit prompt, app or session.
definitions.Aura: The perceptible sense that an artifact or environment holds reachable possibilities beyond what is currently visible.
definitions.Field: A shared condition in which continuity, context and capability are sustained across people, artifacts and environments.

evidence_boundary.describes: A conceptual relationship between scarce human time, limited attention and increasingly abundant machine intelligence.
evidence_boundary.proposes: AI can contribute to more humane environments when it returns attention and sustains continuity.
evidence_boundary.does_not_establish: That Warmth, Ambience, Aura or Field follow automatically from more capable models, or that the full transition has occurred.
